text: Synthetic Smart Wiper System - High-Level Design SYNTHETIC TEST DATA - fictional example for tool testing. Not an official AUTOSAR document and not Tata Technologies material. Document ID: SYN-HLD-WIPER-001. Version: 1.0.
This synthetic High-Level Design describes a fictional Smart Wiper system. It exists only to test the AutoDoc AI tool.
The scope covers rain detection, wiper speed selection, motor driving and fault storage.

WiperControlSwc coordinates the wiper speed request. RainSensorSwc measures rain intensity and provides it through RainSensorInterface. WiperMotorDriverSwc drives the wiper motor and reports faults. VehicleSpeedProviderSwc supplies the vehicle speed. DiagnosticHandlerSwc stores wiper faults.
The port P_RainIntensity is provided by RainSensorSwc. The port R_RainIntensity is required by WiperControlSwc. The signal Sig_RainIntensity is updated every 20 ms.
The port P_MotorCommand is provided by WiperControlSwc. The port R_MotorCommand is required by WiperMotorDriverSwc. The signal Sig_MotorSpeedCmd carries the requested motor speed.
The signal Sig_VehicleSpeed is provided by VehicleSpeedProviderSwc. RainSensorIf is the legacy name used by the diagnostic tooling.

First, RainSensorSwc sends Sig_RainIntensity to WiperControlSwc every 50 ms. Then WiperControlSwc requests the current vehicle speed from VehicleSpeedProviderSwc. Next, WiperControlSwc sends Sig_MotorSpeedCmd to WiperMotorDriverSwc.

If WiperMotorDriverSwc detects an overcurrent, it reports a fault to DiagnosticHandlerSwc. After a fault is reported, DiagnosticHandlerSwc notifies WasherPumpSwc and stores the fault. The WiperMotorDriverSwc performs a self-test at startup.

HLD-FUN-001: WiperControlSwc shall select the wiper speed from the rain intensity. HLD-FUN-002: WiperMotorDriverSwc shall limit the motor current to 8 A. HLD-FUN-002: DiagnosticHandlerSwc shall store each wiper fault.
